channel.title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - Water
channel.description: Curated OT/ICS advisories, incidents and threat intelligence. Editorial by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

item.title: [Critical] Iran-linked hackers locked operators out of control panels at small Midwest water stations, the Wall Street Journal reports, as DHS tells Congress that water is increasingly in Iran-backed hackers’ sights
item.category: Top Story
item.description: The Wall Street Journal reported on 13 November, citing unnamed US and Israeli officials, that since the summer Iran-linked hackers have locked operators out of control panels at water stations in small Midwestern towns, breached networks aboard two Texas-bound energy tankers and sabotaged supermarket refrigeration in Europe. No utility, state or date has been named for the water cases. Check Point’s Sergey Shykevich linked the activity mainly to CyberAv3ngers, which works under Iran’s cyber command, and acting CISA head Nick Andersen named programmable logic controllers as the equipment Iranian actors threaten. On 18 November Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin’s written testimony to the House Homeland Security Committee said Iran-backed actors have targeted US critical infrastructure since February, with water among the sectors increasingly in their sights, and described the attacks so far as mostly localized disruptions of poorly secured control systems. Iran’s ambassador to France denies that Iran carries out cyberattacks abroad. On 23–24 November US officials also told the Journal that Iran is the main suspect in up to 50 attacks on energy tankers (see Threat Intelligence & Research). Separately, Illinois says an attempt on the Algonquin Dam on 16 November was blocked (see Incidents & Attacks). It leads because it is the clearest official signal yet that small, internet-reachable water controllers are the target (editorial assessment). - Wall Street Journal (13 Nov 2026), via Iran International and the Newsmax wire on Yahoo News; DHS Secretary’s written testimony to the House Homeland Security Committee, via the Jerusalem Post (18 Nov 2026); CISA AA26-097A (updated 22 Jul 2026) - WSJ report 13 Nov 2026; testimony 18 Nov 2026; water-station incidents since summer 2026, undated

item.title: [High] Illinois investigates an apparent cyberattack attempt on the Algonquin Dam on the Fox River
item.category: Incident — Attempted cyberattack on the state-run Algonquin Dam, Fox River, Illinois (16 Nov 2026; disclosed by IDNR 20 Nov 2026); dam kept secure and operating; CISA and state agencies investigating; no attribution
item.description: The Illinois Department of Natural Resources said on 20 November that its Office of Water Resources detected an apparent attempted cyberattack on the Algonquin Dam on the Fox River, about 45 miles northwest of Chicago, on 16 November. Staff blocked the unauthorised access at once, and IDNR says the dam stayed secure and fully operational. It has not said which system was targeted or whether gate controls were reachable. Illinois State Police, the Illinois Emergency Management Agency, the state’s technology department and CISA are assisting; IDNR says it has no indication of a link to other recent incidents, and no group has been named. For water-resource and flood-control owners, it is a prompt to check who can reach gate and level controls remotely (editorial assessment). - CBS Chicago (20 Nov 2026); ABC7 Chicago (20–21 Nov 2026); BNO News (21 Nov 2026); Gizmodo (21 Nov 2026, citing the Chicago Tribune); all citing the Illinois Department of Natural Resources - Attempt 16 Nov 2026; disclosed 20 Nov 2026; investigation ongoing

item.title: [High] France expects EU sanctions on 14 December over Iran’s refrigeration sabotage, after CISA and the FBI warned the threat to internet-connected controllers is ongoing
item.category: Incident — Cross-sector attacks on internet-connected refrigeration controllers (France, Oct; about 11 European countries, 1–2 Nov); CISA/FBI joint warning 5 Nov; France attributes the October attack to Iran’s IRGC; EU sanctions expected 14 Dec
item.description: Hackers tampered with web-managed refrigeration controllers at about 700 French sites in October, forcing defrost or heating cycles; French authorities report at least 15 fires, and Paris blames the IRGC’s Shahid Kaveh unit. A second wave on 1–2 November reached about 11 European countries, and on 5 November CISA and the FBI, with HHS, USDA and DOT, warned that the threat is ongoing. France’s foreign minister said on 17 November he expects EU sanctions on 14 December, and EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas has confirmed new Iran sanctions are being prepared; Iran rejects the accusations. Sweden’s NCSC says victims mainly ran older systems with weak passwords. No water utility is reported hit, but exposed controllers with weak passwords and contractor remote access describe many small water sites too (editorial assessment). - Arab News, from AFP (17 Nov 2026, EU decision expected 14 Dec); dpa, via Yahoo News (16 Nov 2026, Kallas); The Record (9 Nov 2026, French attribution and at least 15 fires); TechCrunch (5 Nov 2026, CISA/FBI joint statement); eBuilder Security (11 Nov 2026, Swedish NCSC); CERT-FR CERTFR-2026-ALE-012 - October attack 11–12 Oct 2026; second wave 1–2 Nov 2026; CISA/FBI warning 5 Nov 2026; sanctions statements 16–18 Nov 2026; EU decision expected 14 Dec 2026

item.title: [Critical] Attackers rooted unpatched Check Point gateways through PHP2Shell, planted backdoors and wiped a VMware host; the root flaw is now in KEV
item.category: Incident — PHP2Shell plus Gaia root flaw CVE-2026-123039 used to backdoor Check Point gateways and wipe a VMware ESXi host (wave 1 from 30 Oct, Israel; wave 2 from 2 Nov, multiple countries); CVE-2026-123039 added to CISA KEV 13 Nov 2026
item.description: Check Point Research said on 12 November that attackers exploited the PHP2Shell flaws on unpatched Check Point Mobile Access portals from 30 October, then used a local flaw (CVE-2026-123039) to become root. They planted backdoors, pivoted to a VMware ESXi host and ran a wiper. The first wave hit Israeli organizations, some destructively; a second wave from 2 November reached several countries without destruction. Attribution is unconfirmed (tooling resembles China-nexus UNC5221). CISA added the root flaw to KEV on 13 November. No OT victim is reported, but these firewalls often sit at the IT/OT boundary and ESXi often hosts HMIs and historians (editorial assessment). - Check Point Research (12 Nov 2026); SecurityWeek (13 Nov 2026); Canadian Centre for Cyber Security AV26-1154 (12 Nov 2026, updated 13 Nov); CISA KEV alert (13 Nov 2026); BleepingComputer (Nov 2026) - Wave 1 from 30 Oct 2026; wave 2 from 2 Nov 2026; research published 12 Nov 2026; KEV addition 13 Nov 2026

item.title: [Medium] Bloomberg: Russia-aligned hacktivists have tampered with exposed water and industrial controls since 2024, including a Danish waterworks attack that burst pipes
item.category: Incident review — Russia-aligned hacktivist tampering with exposed water and industrial controls since 2024 (Bloomberg, 27 Oct 2026); Danish attribution of the 2024 Tureby waterworks attack to Z-Pentest
item.description: Bloomberg News published a review on 27 October of a loose network of Russia-sympathetic hackers that it says has carried out hundreds of attacks since 2024 on water plants, factories, dams and similar sites. The best-documented water case is the December 2024 attack on Tureby Alkestrup Waterworks in Køge, Denmark, where the pressure-control system was reset to zero and pipes burst on restart; Denmark’s Defence Intelligence Service attributed it to Z-Pentest in December 2025, and Danish authorities put the impact at about 50 households without water for seven hours. Bloomberg also reports control changes at an unnamed Texas water system in 2024 that spilled reservoir water. The groups’ own claims are unverified. These cases are historical, but they show low-skill tampering with exposed controls can cause physical damage (editorial assessment). - Bloomberg News, 27 Oct 2026 (partly paywalled; summary by Meduza, 28 Oct 2026); Denmark’s Defence Intelligence Service attribution, reported by Euronews, 19 Dec 2025; CISA, FBI, NSA and partners joint advisory, 9 Dec 2025 - Review published 27 Oct 2026; Danish attack Dec 2024, attributed Dec 2025; Texas case 2024

item.title: [Medium] US officials eye Iran in up to 50 cyberattacks on energy tankers, widening the campaign that has already hit small water systems
item.category: Threat intelligence — Wall Street Journal report (23–24 Nov 2026): up to 50 cyberattacks on oil, LNG and chemical tankers; US officials eye Iran, some name Russia; Coast Guard cyber teams boarded at least four vessels; cross-sector item carried for water (editorial assessment)
item.description: US officials told the Wall Street Journal, in a report carried on 23–24 November, that Iran is the main suspect in as many as 50 cyberattacks on tankers carrying oil, liquefied gas and chemicals. The Coast Guard has sent cyber teams to at least four vessels nearing US shores, including the Texas-bound VL Prosperity and Kohaku, and the VL Prosperity’s captain received a ransom note. Some officials also name Russia, one administration official called four of the attacks a minor nuisance, and no ship is reported disabled. Water is not a target in this report, but it is the same period and, officials suspect, the same state sponsor as the water-station lockouts in the top story. Water utilities should expect the same tactics against their own exposed controllers and edge firewalls (editorial assessment). - Reuters, via US News (23 Nov 2026, WSJ report); Israel Hayom (24 Nov 2026); heise online (24 Nov 2026) - WSJ report 23 Nov 2026; follow-up coverage 24 Nov 2026; investigations ongoing, no formal US attribution

item.title: [High] Lumen: Volt Typhoon’s “Silent Train” network has reached targets since 2023 through hijacked routers and flaws in management platforms, and lists water among the sectors hit
item.category: Research — China-linked relay network and management-platform exploitation; water among the named sectors; no OT intrusion described
item.description: Lumen’s Black Lotus Labs reported on 28 October on Silent Train, a framework it attributes to Volt Typhoon, the group US agencies link to the Chinese state, and has seen in consistent use since November 2023. For each operation the operators build a single-use chain, from virtual private servers outside the US through hijacked home-office routers and IoT devices abroad and then in the US, sometimes in under two minutes, and take it apart afterwards, which makes the traffic hard to trace or block. The chains are used to reach targets and exploit IT and network management platforms: Lumen ties the group to flaws in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN (CVE-2026-20127, CVSS v3.1 10.0, Cisco), VeloCloud Orchestrator (CVE-2026-16812), N-able N-central (CVE-2025-8875 and CVE-2025-8876) and Versa Director, and likely an undisclosed Quest KACE flaw. Its key findings list water among the critical-infrastructure sectors affected, alongside energy, transportation, maritime, rail, aviation and emergency services; Lumen says it has notified hundreds of victims over three years, and Hawaii, California and Texas were the most targeted states. No victim is named and no intrusion into OT is described. These are different flaws from the VeloCloud and Cisco SD-WAN Manager bugs on other cards on this page. In our assessment, these platforms are what a utility’s IT or network provider uses to manage every site at once, so a compromise there reaches all of them. - Lumen Black Lotus Labs, 28 Oct 2026 (primary); Zero Day (Kim Zetter) and CyberScoop, 28 Oct 2026; KEV dates from CISA’s 30 Oct 2026 catalog - Activity since Nov 2023; report published 28 Oct 2026

item.title: [Medium] Dragos counts 1,266 industrial ransomware attacks in Q3, four of them at water utilities, and found no operator touching a control system
item.category: Research — Dragos Industrial Ransomware Analysis for Q3 2026 (published 16 Nov 2026), covering July–September; Check Point October 2026 statistics (12 Nov 2026) for comparison
item.description: Dragos said on 16 November that ransomware hit 1,266 industrial organizations between July and September 2026, up 11% from 1,140 in the second quarter, and the number of brands claiming industrial victims rose from 70 to 99. Manufacturing took 69% of cases; Dragos lists four water-utility incidents and seven at electric utilities. Qilin and The Gentlemen led the claims. Dragos found no Q3 case of a ransomware operator manipulating a control system: production stopped because the IT, ERP and virtualization layers that plants depend on went down, as when Fairlife halted all four of its US plants for about 11 days. Entry came through edge devices and enterprise applications exploited within days of disclosure, and through stolen VPN and firewall credentials. For utilities, the practical risk is losing billing, SCADA servers or historians hosted on shared IT infrastructure (editorial assessment). - Dragos (16 Nov 2026); Australian Cyber Security Magazine (17 Nov 2026); Check Point Research October 2026 statistics, via iTWire (12 Nov 2026) - Published 16 Nov 2026; data covers July–September 2026

item.title: [Info] Indiana water utilities weigh PLC exposure against small budgets as a state law extends cyber duties to systems serving 500 people
item.category: Sector reporting — Indiana water and wastewater utilities; state law SEA 459 (2025); no new incident
item.description: An Indianapolis Business Journal feature, republished by The Republic on 14 November, looks at how Indiana water and wastewater utilities are handling cyber risk. Senate Enrolled Act 459, passed in 2025, requires covered utilities to run annual cybersecurity evaluations, name a state cybersecurity contact and report incidents, and lowers the threshold to utilities serving at least 500 people from 3,300. A lawyer quoted estimates that about 80% of water and wastewater infrastructure is run by local governments with few dedicated security staff; Tipton pays about $25,000 up front and $5,000 a year for contracted security services. Indiana’s drinking-water cybersecurity lead said one activity reported during the summer campaign caused no disruption and may have been federal scanning. Interviewees named exposed PLCs as the main risk and warned that falsified monitoring data could lead operators to react to conditions that are not happening. - The Republic / Indianapolis Business Journal (14 Nov 2026); Security Boulevard, Daily OT Security News (15 Nov 2026) - Published 14 Nov 2026; SEA 459 enacted 2025

item.title: [Medium] Claroty finds 65,000 game consoles, smart speakers and cars on critical-infrastructure networks, most of them on production segments
item.category: Research — Claroty analysis of 45 million devices at 30,000+ critical-infrastructure sites (released 17 Nov 2026); no CVE IDs published
item.description: Claroty said on 17 November that, across 45 million devices at more than 30,000 critical-infrastructure sites, it found about 65,000 consumer gadgets that do not belong on operational networks: game consoles, smart-home and entertainment devices, and connected cars. Industrial sites had 963 game consoles, nearly 90% of them on production rather than guest networks, and thousands of connected vehicles were attached to site networks with almost none isolated on a guest segment. Claroty did not break the figures out for water utilities. At treatment plants and pump stations where the plant network, office Wi-Fi and staff devices share switches, each unmanaged gadget is a foothold that quietly undermines the segmentation SCADA depends on (editorial assessment). - Claroty press release, via PR Newswire (17 Nov 2026); Facilities Dive (18 Nov 2026); Help Net Security (19 Nov 2026) - Research released 17 Nov 2026

item.title: [Critical] PHP2Shell attacks rooted about two dozen Palo Alto firewalls, and Siemens, Schneider and ABB now list grid-control, DCS and RTU products, several with no fix
item.category: Active exploitation — PHP2Shell chained with a Linux kernel flaw to root exposed PAN-OS firewalls, 23–24 Oct; OT vendor advisories 28–30 Oct; Siemens adds metering gateways 16 Nov
item.description: Palo Alto’s Unit 42 verified that a suspected China-nexus actor chained the PHP2Shell flaws (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) with Linux kernel bug CVE-2026-46300 to root about two dozen internet-exposed PAN-OS firewalls on 23–24 October and steal Active Directory credentials. Siemens (Spectrum Power, AMIS TS and, since 16 November, WTV676/WTV776 metering gateways), Schneider (a Foxboro DCS server) and ABB (Netcontrol RTUs, ASPECT gateways) now list affected products, several unfixed. None is reported exploited and no OT operator is named: treat it as an IT-to-OT boundary warning. - Unit 42 (updated 29 Oct 2026); Palo Alto Networks advisory for CVE-2026-109618 (updated 29 Oct 2026); The Record (29 Oct 2026) and Infosecurity Magazine (30 Oct 2026), citing Dream; CISA KEV catalog (30 Oct 2026 release); Siemens SSA-166980 V1.4 (16 Nov 2026, WTV676/WTV776 added; V1.2 29 Oct 2026), SSA-566512 V1.1 (28 Oct 2026), SSA-019113 and SSA-082556; Schneider Electric SESB-2026-295-01 v3.2.0 (30 Oct 2026); ABB Netcontrol and Arctic advisories (30 Oct 2026), ASPECT advisory (29 Oct 2026) and APROL SA26P015 (23 Oct 2026); CERT@VDE VDE-2026-127 and VDE-2026-137 - Root compromises 23–24 Oct 2026, verified by Unit 42 29 Oct 2026; KEV additions 26 and 28 Oct 2026; Siemens, Schneider and ABB updates 28–30 Oct 2026; Siemens metering gateways added 16 Nov 2026

item.title: [High] A vCenter authentication bypass was exploited as a zero-day for two months before Broadcom’s 19 November patch; vCenter 7.0 gets no fix
item.category: Active exploitation — VMware vCenter authentication bypass CVE-2026-123890 (CVSS 9.8) exploited as a zero-day for more than two months by a suspected China-linked group, per Mandiant; Broadcom fix released 19 Nov 2026; no public fix for vCenter 7.0
item.description: Broadcom patched CVE-2026-123890 on 19 November, a critical flaw in vCenter’s directory service that lets a remote, unauthenticated attacker obtain an administrator session. Google’s Mandiant, which reported the bug, says a suspected China-linked espionage group it tracks as Armory Castle (formerly UNC5221, also called Warp Panda) exploited it for more than two months beforehand. In the incidents Mandiant investigated, the group got in through a BeyondTrust Remote Support flaw, moved to Linux appliances, attacked vCenter in early September with a custom tool called Bonesaw, stole SAML signing material and the vCenter master key, created an SSO admin account, forged tokens and moved on to ESXi hosts. Fixes are in vCenter 9.1.1.0200, 9.0.2.0200 and 8.0 U3m; end-of-life vCenter 7.0 has no public patch. No victims or sectors are named. Many plants run HMIs, historians and engineering workstations as virtual machines, so whoever controls vCenter controls those hosts (editorial assessment). - SecurityWeek (19 Nov 2026, citing Broadcom, Google Threat Intelligence/Mandiant and Mandiant CTO Charles Carmakal); CISA KEV alert (20 Nov 2026); The Hacker News (20–21 Nov 2026) - Added to CISA KEV 20 Nov 2026; patched 19 Nov 2026; exploited from at least early Sep 2026

item.title: [High] N-able ships Hotfix 3 for 17 more N-central flaws after attackers planted miners on servers already running Hotfix 2
item.category: Active exploitation — N-able N-central: 4EverAble2Shell exploited to plant miners (13 Nov 2026); N-central 2026.4 Hotfix 3 fixes 17 more CVEs and removes the Legacy API (16–17 Nov 2026); separate breach of N-able’s hosted Mail Assure/SpamExperts cloud disclosed 20 Nov 2026
item.description: N-able released N-central 2026.4 Hotfix 3 on 16 November, which it calls a critical security update. It fixes 17 new CVEs, including authentication bypasses, missing authorization checks, path traversal leading to code execution and a syslog injection that runs commands as root, and it removes the Legacy API option that the actively exploited 4EverAble2Shell chain depends on. On-premises servers need the upgrade now; hosted servers update automatically, but every customer must also upgrade Agents and Probes, which N-able warns can otherwise be impersonated. The fix follows Huntback’s 13 November finding of cryptocurrency miners on 21 N-central servers, 19 of them on Hotfix 2. Remote control and Intune integration stay blocked for now. Separately, N-able said on 20 November that attackers reached a server in its hosted Mail Assure and SpamExperts email-filtering cloud, forcing it to take the management portal and APIs offline; it says mail flow continued, it has found no access to customer data, and the breach is unrelated to N-central. Many integrators manage plant-side Windows hosts through RMM tools, and a miner today can be a hands-on intruder tomorrow (editorial assessment). - BleepingComputer (20 Nov 2026, Mail Assure/SpamExperts breach); The Hacker News (17 Nov 2026, Hotfix 3, citing N-able release notes of 16 Nov); The Hacker News (13 Nov 2026, citing Huntback and Previdian); The Hacker News (12 Nov 2026, new chains); SecurityWeek (13 Nov 2026); Tenable (10 Nov 2026) - Mail Assure breach disclosed 20 Nov 2026; Hotfix 3 released 16 Nov 2026; exploitation reported 13 Nov 2026; Able2Shell disclosed 9 Nov 2026

item.title: [High] Attackers root clustered Cisco Expressway gateways soon after a public exploit, and CISA adds the flaw to KEV
item.category: Active exploitation — Cisco Expressway CVE-2026-76466 (CVSS 9.8), clustered Expressway Core/Edge; exploited after a public PoC (reported by F6); added to CISA KEV 20 Nov 2026; fixed in X15.5.20
item.description: Security firm F6 says attackers exploited CVE-2026-76466, a critical flaw in clustered Cisco Expressway Core and Edge deployments, shortly after proof-of-concept code appeared on GitHub. They broke into two internet-facing Expressway nodes at an unnamed Russian organization, moved to more cluster nodes inside the network and gained root, then ran scripts to scan for SMB shares, SQL Server and WinRM hosts and to hunt for credentials. CISA added the flaw to its KEV catalog on 20 November. Cisco fixed it on 21 October; there is no workaround. No water utility or OT victim is reported. Larger utilities and city IT departments that run Expressway for remote calling should treat an exposed, unpatched cluster as a foothold close to SCADA and plant networks (editorial assessment; cross-sector item carried for water). - Security Affairs (21 Nov 2026, CISA KEV additions of 20 Nov); SecurityWeek (Nov 2026, citing F6) - Added to CISA KEV 20 Nov 2026; exploitation reported 18–20 Nov 2026; patched 21 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] Java4Shell exploitation attempts begin, and Siemens tells customers to take Industrial Edge Management offline until patched
item.category: Advisory — OpenJDK “Java4Shell” memory-corruption flaw CVE-2026-114938 (disclosed and patched 17 Nov 2026); exploitation attempts seen 18–19 Nov 2026; Siemens SSA-272816 lists three Industrial Edge Management products
item.description: Probing for Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938), a memory-corruption bug in how OpenJDK 17.0.6 and later decode Base64 data, started within two days of its 17 November disclosure. GreyNoise counted more than 150 matching requests from five addresses by early 19 November and Previdian logged nine attempts from six addresses; none is confirmed to have succeeded. Exploitation needs a recent Intel or AMD x86-64 processor with AVX-512 VBMI, and researchers at Calif showed unauthenticated code execution against default Jira, Confluence, Jenkins and Keycloak setups, each with a tailored chain. For OT teams the key item is Siemens advisory SSA-272816: three Industrial Edge Management products are affected, fixes are in progress, and Siemens recommends taking those instances offline until they are patched. Cisco lists more than a dozen products with no fix yet, and Atlassian Data Center products are also unpatched. - SecurityWeek (19 Nov 2026, citing Calif, GreyNoise, WatchTowr, Cloudflare, Previdian, Siemens SSA-272816, Cisco and Atlassian); The Record (18 Nov 2026, CISA alert) - Disclosed and patched 17 Nov 2026; exploitation attempts 18–19 Nov 2026

item.title: [High] November ICS patches: Siemens flags high-severity flaws in SIMATIC SCADA, PCS 7 and WinCC Graphics Designer, several without fixes, plus Node2Shell exposure
item.category: Advisory — ICS Patch Tuesday, 10–11 Nov 2026: Siemens, Schneider Electric, Phoenix Contact, Hitachi Energy and others; Node.js Node2Shell CVE-2026-111497 in CISA KEV since 27 Oct 2026; Updated 24 Nov 2026: CISA republished the Schneider Rapsody advisory as ICSA-26-328-02
item.description: Siemens published nine advisories covering ten vulnerabilities on November’s ICS Patch Tuesday, SecurityWeek reported on 11 November. High-severity issues affect SIMATIC SCADA and PCS 7, SIMATIC WinCC Graphics Designer, the IOT2050 platform, ROS#, Simcenter Femap and the Mendix Studio Pro MCP server, and Siemens says patches are not yet available for several products, with some versions never to be fixed. Two further Siemens advisories cover exposure to Node2Shell (CVE-2026-111497), an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder used by Node.js that CISA added to its KEV catalog on 27 October; exploitation attempts have been seen, but none aimed at Siemens products. Phoenix Contact and Hitachi Energy confirmed products affected by PHP2Shell, and Schneider Electric fixed a file-handling flaw in EcoStruxure Power Build Rapsody, which CISA republished as ICSA-26-328-02 on 24 November. On 17 November CISA republished the Brotli assessment as ICSA-26-321-03, naming WinCC V7/V8, WinCC Runtime Professional, WinCC OA and TIA Administrator; fixes exist only for BRAUMAT/SISTAR and WinCC OA V3.20, so most WinCC sites must rely on disabling Brotli for now. WinCC and PCS 7 run HMI and SCADA screens at many water and wastewater plants (editorial assessment). - SecurityWeek, ICS Patch Tuesday (11 Nov 2026); CISA ICSA-26-321-03 (17 Nov 2026); CISA ICSA-26-328-02 (24 Nov 2026); BleepingComputer (28 Oct 2026, Node2Shell KEV addition); Siemens ProductCERT November 2026 advisories - Advisories published 10–11 Nov 2026; CISA republications 17 and 24 Nov 2026; Node2Shell in KEV 27 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] CISA republishes Mitsubishi Electric’s ICONICS advisory: fixes for GENESIS64 and GENESIS, none for MC Works64, GENESIS32 or BizViz
item.category: Advisory — Critical-rated flaws in ICONICS SCADA, HMI and historian software, now republished by CISA; no fix for three older products
item.description: CISA republished Mitsubishi Electric advisory 2026-006 as ICSA-26-300-02 on 27 October, twelve days after the vendor released it. It covers flaws across Mitsubishi’s ICONICS SCADA, HMI and historian products. The highest-rated, CVE-2026-16438 (CVSS v3.1 9.1 in Mitsubishi’s advisory), gives the administrator account default DCOM permissions. CVE-2026-16436 (v3.1 8.1) is a shared, fixed challenge-response that can unlock any user account once an attacker obtains the response; the advisory also lists a second challenge-response flaw, CVE-2026-16437 (v3.1 6.4), and the older libwebp bug CVE-2023-4863 (v3.1 8.2). Affected are GENESIS up to 11.03 and GENESIS64, ICONICS Suite, Hyper Historian, AnalytiX, MobileHMI and IoTWorX up to 10.97.3; version 10.98 and GENESIS 11.04 fix them (10.97.3 for libwebp). MC Works64, GENESIS32 and BizViz, all versions, will get no fix, and Mitsubishi advises replacing them with GENESIS64 or GENESIS. None of the ICONICS-specific flaws is in KEV; the bundled libwebp flaw CVE-2023-4863 has been in KEV since 13 September 2023 from browser exploitation. No exploitation of ICONICS products is reported. CISA’s republication lists only Critical Manufacturing as the sector, but GENESIS64 also runs SCADA and HMI screens in water and wastewater (editorial assessment). - Mitsubishi Electric PSIRT advisory 2026-006, 15 Oct 2026 (primary); CISA ICSA-26-300-02, 27 Oct 2026, via the CIRCL vulnerability database; CIRCL record for CVE-2023-4863 (KEV entry) - Vendor advisory 15 Oct 2026; CISA republication 27 Oct 2026

item.title: [Info] The Water Watch Center now gives free security monitoring and help to water utilities in 26 states
item.category: Policy & support — NRWA and DEF CON Franklin Water Watch Center (launched Aug 2026); free monitoring now in 26 states (announced 20 Nov 2026); no CVE
item.description: The Water Watch Center, a joint effort of the National Rural Water Association and the volunteer hacker group DEF CON Franklin, said on Friday 20 November that it is providing free security monitoring and assistance to water utilities in 26 states, Cybersecurity Dive reported on 23 November. Launched in August, the center pays security firms, including Rapid7, Defendify, Legato Security, TPO Group and BlastWave, to give rural utilities free intrusion detection and defensive consultations. Nearly 100 utilities have contacted it so far. It is funded by grants from Craig Newmark Philanthropies, the Hewlett Foundation and DARPA. For small systems with no security staff it is one of the few no-cost ways to get eyes on the network; the limit is staff time to install sensors and act on alerts (editorial assessment). - Cybersecurity Dive (Eric Geller, 23 Nov 2026); Water Watch Center announcement (20 Nov 2026) - Announced 20 Nov 2026; reported 23 Nov 2026; center launched Aug 2026

item.title: [Info] Texas Cyber Command signs up 63 companies to give Texas water and wastewater utilities free security help under Project Watershed 250
item.category: Regulation & Policy — Project Watershed 250 (federal–Texas six-month pilot launched 31 Aug 2026); first partner cohort of 63 companies reported 18 Nov 2026
item.description: Texas Cyber Command has brought 63 technology and cybersecurity companies into Project Watershed 250, the six-month pilot launched on 31 August by the White House Office of the National Cyber Director with the Texas governor’s office, GovTech reported on 18 November. Partners named include Palo Alto Networks, Cisco, Cloudflare, Akamai, Tenable, AWS, Claroty and Elisity, covering OT and ICS visibility, enterprise security tools, assessments and remediation at no cost; utilities choose which services to use, and Dispel said on 19 November it is offering OT remote access. Texas has about 7,400 public water systems and 3,000 wastewater treatment facilities. No participation numbers or results have been published, and partners are still working out what can be delivered quickly and how services continue after the pilot. - GovTech (18 Nov 2026); Dispel release via EIN Presswire (19 Nov 2026, sponsored); Texas Cyber Command, Project Watershed 250 - Pilot launched 31 Aug 2026; partner cohort reported 18 Nov 2026

item.title: [Info] Comments close 30 November on NIST’s draft rewrite of its OT security guide, which adds water, food, rail, maritime and building-automation coverage
item.category: Guidance — NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 4 draft (released 21 Sep 2026); public comments close 30 Nov 2026; no CVE
item.description: NIST’s draft Revision 4 of SP 800-82, the US government’s main guide to operational technology security, is open for public comment until 30 November 2026. The draft reorganises the guide around Cybersecurity Framework 2.0, with risk management now led by the Govern function, and adds sector material for building automation, water and wastewater, food and agriculture, freight rail, maritime vessels, and industrial IoT connected to cloud services. It also expands guidance on asset management, network monitoring and detection, protecting system-management functions, and applying zero-trust principles. Many regulators, insurers and auditors use 800-82 as a reference, so its final wording can shape what operators are asked to show; the comment window is the chance for practitioners to flag guidance that would not work on a plant floor. - NIST CSRC, SP 800-82 Rev. 4 initial public draft (21 Sep 2026); SecurityWeek (24 Sep 2026); OT Security Wire (14 Nov 2026, summary of the draft) - Draft 21 Sep 2026; summarised 14 Nov 2026; forward-looking: public comments close 30 Nov 2026
